purpose: Upgrade entry-count divergence to sense-unit comparison and publish an honest, source-traceable inventory audit.

sampleDesign.disparityDefinition: The committed sense-depth top-200 gaps (largest max-min sense-unit spread); disparity-enriched, not a random population sample.
sampleDesign.coverageDefinition: Deterministic SHA-256 sample within nCoreDicts strata from the microstructure-profile universe (lemmas in >=2 of MW, AP, PWG, PWK, WIL, VCP, SKD), excluding disparity lemmas.

humanGold.reason: This unattended unit cannot run two blind human keys and adjudication. The published 500-lemma sample carries two automated keys (MW validated section adapter and MW gloss-clause splitter) and an explicit unadjudicated label; no human κ is claimed.
humanGold.requiredForFullAcceptance: Two blind human keys plus source-line adjudication on the 500-lemma sample.

h5950.reused: External task framing and the instruction not to rebuild the B3 inventory.
h5950.newHere: Cross-dictionary sense-unit evidence from csl-atlas dictionaries.

h6843.reused: External MW sense-inventory prior art; no MW inventory duplicated.
h6843.newHere: Cross-dictionary audit and structural disagreement metrics.

reconciliation.boundary: No WSD model, classifier, DCS ingestion, or B3 inventory rebuild in this unit.

dominantSecondary.definition: Dominant = dictionary with the most sense units for a lemma; secondary = second most. Rates use lemmas present in >=2 core sense-segmented dictionaries.

disagreement.definition: Disagreement = the core dictionaries do not all report the same sense-unit count for the lemma. This is structural, not semantic, disagreement.

doubleKey.keyB: independent gloss-clause splitter (semicolon boundaries in MW body text)
doubleKey.note: Automated coding agreement, not human inter-annotator kappa. The two keys read the same source text with independently implemented segmenters; they are not independent human annotators.

notMeasurable.superset: R2 anchor alignments expose a Jaccard score and shared anchors, not full MWSA sense sets; superset/subset cannot be asserted without the MWSA inventory.
notMeasurable.subset: R2 anchor alignments expose a Jaccard score and shared anchors, not full MWSA sense sets; superset/subset cannot be asserted without the MWSA inventory.

elexisMwsa.reason: No ELEXIS MWSA relation inventory is checked into csl-atlas or present in the local workspace; external evaluation is therefore an honest null, not a fabricated match.

isclsWsd.reason: Cited for the WSD task framing; this audit does not build or evaluate a WSD model.

isclsMwSenseInventory.reason: Cited as external MW sense-inventory prior art; no MW-specific sense inventory is duplicated here.

limitations: The disparity stratum is the committed top-200 sense-depth gap list, not a random sample; population inference is limited to the stated strata.

Cross-dictionary sense units exist only where validated adapters exist (MW, AP, PWG, PWK core; broad adapters where committed). WIL, VCP and SKD have no sense adapter, so they contribute entry coverage but not sense units.
Sense units are structural section/marker counts, not curated semantic senses; labels such as 'dominant' mean 'most sense sections', not 'most meanings'.
MW live recomputation requires a local csl-orig checkout; when it is absent the MW double-key is reported as unavailable.
The reported kappa is automated coding agreement between two segmenter implementations on MW, not human inter-annotator agreement.
No ELEXIS MWSA inventory is available locally, so external MWSA (=, superset, subset, related) evaluation is an honest null; only = and related are measured on internal R2 anchor alignments.
Sense counts may be inflated by dictionary-specific subsection markers (e.g. PWG/PWK <div> blocks); method IDs are recorded per dictionary.
